audit.whatIsWrong: Four rows contradicted both the packet chart and their own why-text: Level 3 read Poppy while whys[2] says 'it's skill'; Level 6 read Skill while whys[4] says 'Level 6 hands it to Cho'; First item read Poppy while whys[5] says 'he owns the all-in'; 2+ items read Poppy while whys[6] says 'reads even again'.
audit.why: Packet chart is Skill/Poppy/Skill/Skill/Cho'Gath/Cho'Gath/Skill, and the mirror audit has already proposed exactly that group on Cho'Gath's side — so this is the chart both directions must show.
audit.corrected: Rows 2, 4, 5 and 6 flipped in both layers as one group, with ratings dropped on the two rows he now owns.

audit.why: Rupture is a flat 6s, Feral Scream 11s at rank 1, Feast 80/70/60 — the 80s R is the timer the whole mid-game plan turns on.
audit.corrected: 6s, 11s and 80s written into dosFull[0], dontsFull[1], dontsFull[2], the cooldown block, report[5], spikes[1] and whys[4].

audit.whatIsWrong: Three problems. Feast was described as trading in lane at levels 2-3 — it is his ultimate and does not exist before 6. Feast was twice called a 'percent-HP execute'; Riot's text says high true damage, and growth only if the target dies. And the boilerplate 'W any dash he tries' is inert: Cho'Gath has no dash in his kit.
audit.why: Riot's text: Q ruptures and knocks up (6s), W is a cone silence (11s), E is an on-attack spike slow, R devours for high true damage. The silence and the knockup both cancel Keeper's Verdict, which is the interaction that actually matters and was absent.
audit.corrected: Feast restricted to level 6 and described as true damage that resistances cannot answer; his early trade tools named as Vorpal Spikes and Feral Scream; the dash-stop clause replaced with something true; the channel cancel written in.

audit.whatIsWrong: The build advice is pure armour and MR with no acknowledgement that Feast bypasses both.
audit.why: True damage means Thornmail and Frozen Heart do nothing about his kill button.
audit.corrected: Stated in dontsFull[2] and the cooldown block rather than rewriting the item line, which has no room in band.

edits.before: Level 1 is a wash — you have one ability and his Q knockup outranges your reach, so just farm. From Level 2 you get your real tool: E him into the side wall for a stun, then Q for max-HP damage; that combo doesn't care about your gold and chunks him before his Feast stacks. Dodge his slow-moving Q knockup — if it misses, his W silence and Feast bite have nothing to chain into, and you win the trade clean.
edits.after: Level 1 is a wash — you have one ability and Rupture's 950 range outreaches you, so just farm. From Level 2 you get your real tool: E him into the side wall for a stun, then Q for max-HP damage; that combo doesn't care about your gold. Rupture is a flat 6s and telegraphed — dodge it and his Feral Scream silence has nothing to chain into, and you win the trade clean.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 stay even: your flat damage doesn't scale with points the way his Feast and ability ranks do, so lean on Q chunks and resets rather than hunting a kill. At 6 the lane tilts to him — his R is a true-damage percent-HP execute that ignores every point of armor and MR your W gives you, so even when you out-trade his basics, never sit low in his R range. Keep trading off his Q cooldown, but respect that one knockup-W-bite-R chain can delete you from full-ish HP.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay even: your flat damage doesn't scale the way his ability ranks do, so lean on Q chunks and resets rather than hunting a kill. At 6 the lane tilts to him — Feast is true damage on 80s and ignores every point of armour and MR your W gives you, so never sit low in its 175 range. Keep trading in the 6s gap after Rupture, but respect that knockup into silence into Feast deletes you from full-ish HP.

notes: Feast was being treated as a lane-phase trading tool at levels 2-3 in two places — it is his ultimate and does not exist until 6. It was also twice called a percent-HP execute; Riot's text says high true damage with growth only on a kill, so I wrote 'true damage that resistances do not answer' instead. Confirming the mirror's wider point: Steadfast Presence's dash-stop clause is boilerplate here and inert, because Cho'Gath has no dash — I replaced the one place it read as advice. Four chart rows disagreed with their own why-text and with the packet; flipped as one group to match what the mirror already proposed.
